name: Liquid Motion
visualIdentity: Droplets and viscous forms stretch, string, merge, split, and settle elastically. Choose a coherent 2D or 3D surface treatment; keep highlights from obscuring contours. Metaballs create a fluid appearance, not validated fluid physics. Accurate lettering should be real text held after formation.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to logo formations and abstract transitions; also fits soft 3D, organic illustration, and material transformations. Interactive impact-and-growth scenes suit it when the metaphor and assets support them. For HTML, a WebGL canvas can form the liquid while DOM text takes over after formation. These are suitability judgments, not guarantees.
limitations: Avoid when ambient floating or parallax is all the scene needs, the metaphor is unsupported, or growth would imply false science or hide labels. Metaballs and SDFs do not establish physical fluid behavior; use a simulated and baked Blender workflow for physical splashes or collisions. SDF lettering may not remain legible.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. The optional reference example uses background #171E2B, foreground #F5ECE0, accents #758FC0 and #C889A6; gradients are disabled. Exact task, brand, reference, and semantic colors take precedence; preserve roles and approved colors. Resolve subject colors from the chosen reference, keep lighting coherent, and check contrast in the composited scene.
motionAndInteraction: Use time-driven stretch, merge, split, and elastic settling; a drop may land, spread, and gather into a wordmark, then hold. Optional Immersive Float interaction starts on click/tap or keyboard activation, sequences hover, drop, contact compression, and outward growth, and retains the completed state on pointer exit. Scroll-driven chapters or storytelling are optional only when the narrative needs them; reverse progress should restore matching states. For video, derive states from seekable composition time, not live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, voiceover, or silence for the topic and requirements. A supplied track may drive precomputed beat timing; only major beats should trigger merges or splits. Avoid jitter and preserve speech clarity; synchronize and mix in the render pipeline.
assetRequirements: Use supplied artwork, exact copy, fonts, and authorized audio. For real 3D choose suitable geometry and lighting; for 2D use authored contours or metaballs. Composite real text after formation when precise lettering matters. Physical splashes require simulation and baked assets. Preserve source colors and geometry; prepare or cache topology-changing merges and stateful simulations. Interactive patterns need a receiving surface and impact point; verify direct and backward seeks.
combinations: Optional style-093 kinetic typography gives formed liquid a crisp, readable wordmark; keep type rigid after handoff and highlights clear of letter contours. Optional style-105 can map a supplied music track to deterministic liquid events, with only major beats triggering changes. Do not add these without the relevant text or supplied track. Chapter transitions and scroll storytelling are optional narrative structures, not required liquid treatments.
productionApproach: Choose the renderer and motion method for the desired fidelity: WebGL/GLSL and Three.js support procedural or 3D rendering; optional p5.js can draw stylized blobs, and Paper.js can animate prepared vector contours. These are choices, not a required bundle or physics solver. Keep one owner per animated property and derive states from requested composition time. HyperFrames owns assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, recording the reason. The pipeline must not determine the visual method.
